_comment: Every tunable setting in Vessel is declared here, not in UI code. The
container editor renders this file with one composable per param type, so
adding a knob is a data change. Defaults are correct for the canoe target
'help' is shown next to the control. It must be one plain sentence that a
user who does not know what a translator is can act on. If a setting
cannot be explained that way, it does not belong in this file at all.
For params of type 'component', the default is a selector, not a package
id: '@latest' resolves to the newest installed package of componentType.
Package ids are build outputs (dxvk-2.7.1-canoe) and must never be
hardcoded here, or a version bump would silently break every default.

groups.title: Memory ordering
groups.help: This phone's CPU does not have the hardware mode that makes x86 memory rules free, so FEX has to enforce them itself. These settings trade speed against the risk of glitches in multi-threaded programs, and they matter more here than anywhere else.
groups._advancedNote: Every default in this group is the safe one, and every change to any of them is a trade the user is asked to make blind — 'raise this if a program hangs at random' is a debugging instruction, not a setting. It stays in the product because a maintainer chasing a specific hang needs it, and it stays behind the disclosure because nobody else should meet it.

params.title: Strict memory ordering
params.help: Keep this on: turning it off is faster but breaks most multi-threaded programs.
params.warnText: Most programs will crash or corrupt data with this off.

params.title: Cheap ordering barriers
params.help: Uses a lighter method to enforce memory ordering; leave on unless a program misbehaves.

params.title: Ordering for vector memory
params.help: Very slow in games and rarely needed; turn on only to fix a specific graphical or audio corruption.

params.title: GPU driver
params.help: Turnip is the open driver this app builds for your Adreno 829; the system driver is missing features that most games need.

params.title: Direct3D translation
params.help: Converts the game's Direct3D calls to Vulkan; must match your GPU driver.
params._advancedNote: '@latest' resolves to the one DXVK build published for this device, and the only other honest value is a pin to an older one for a rollback. There is no choice to offer a user here, and the row's own help sentence says the value must match the driver — a control whose correct setting is 'whatever the other control implies' is a readout.

params.title: Driver mode
params.help: Leave on automatic unless a game shows corruption; forcing a mode is a troubleshooting step, not a speed-up.
params._note: CORRECTION (verified in Turnip source, 2026-08-07). An earlier version of this file said GMEM was broken on this GPU and sysmem was mandatory. That is wrong, and it was wrong in both directions. The GMEM page-fault report is scoped to Adreno *830*, not 829, and Turnip does not set disable_gmem for a829 — so forcing sysmem here would give up tiled rendering the hardware can actually do. The Chinese-guide advice to force gmem is equally unfounded: it is Adreno 710/720 guidance. Neither forcing is justified without measuring on this device. Prefer turnip.TU_AUTOTUNE_ALGO, which keeps both modes available and lets the driver choose.

params.title: Rendering mode preference
params.help: Nudges the driver toward direct rendering, which fixes most corruption, while still letting it use the faster tiled path when it is confident.
params._note: Preferred over forcing TU_DEBUG=sysmem: Turnip's own docs note this still allows the other mode in high-confidence cases, so it is a nudge rather than a veto.

params.title: Resolution
params.help: Lower resolutions gain a lot of performance on this phone; it has a smaller GPU cache than the full-size chip.

params.title: Frame rate limit
params.help: Capping frame rate keeps the phone cool, which keeps performance steady over a long session.

groups.title: System
groups._advancedNote: Both settings here have exactly one correct value on this device and the manifest already knows it: esync is the only Wine sync that works without /dev/ntsync, and this chip has no efficiency cluster for a core restriction to avoid. Neither changes anything a user would notice, which is the test for staying on the default screen.

params.title: Thread synchronisation
params.help: esync is the working option on this phone; ntsync needs kernel support Android does not ship yet.

params.title: CPU cores
params.help: This phone has no slow cores, so restricting to the two fastest only helps programs that use a single core.
params._note: Verified on device: cpu0-5 run at 3.32 GHz and cpu6-7 at 3.80 GHz, all Oryon. There is no efficiency cluster, so the usual 'pin to cores 4-7' advice from big.LITTLE devices does not apply. Leave on 'all' until profiling says otherwise.
